title: Learn UI/UX Design
tagline: From first wireframe to systems and flows people can actually use
description: A three-level curriculum for UI/UX Designers. Learn visual fundamentals and Figma, then design systems and interaction, then ship with product and engineering — accessible, consistent interfaces with a documented process, not just pretty screens.
prerequisites: Comfort using a computer and learning a professional design tool
Willingness to show work in progress and take critique
A product you use often enough to notice what is confusing

levels.title: Visual Design & Figma Foundations
levels.goal: Comfortable designing clear static screens and simple flows in Figma

topics.title: Hierarchy, type & color
items: Type scale, weight, and line length for UI
Color: brand, semantic (success/error), and contrast
Spacing, alignment, and grouping so screens scan

topics.title: Layout & composition
items: Grids, margins, and consistent spacing systems
Mobile-first vs. desktop: density and thumb zones
Cards vs. lists vs. tables — pick the pattern for the job

topics.title: Frames, auto-layout & components
items: Frames vs. groups; constraints for resize
Auto-layout for rows, stacks, and padding
Components, variants, and when to detach

topics.title: From wireframe to mock
items: Low-fidelity first: boxes and labels before polish
Hi-fi: applying type, color, and real copy
Naming layers and pages so a teammate can open the file

topics.title: Common screens
items: Onboarding, login, home, list, detail, and forms
Empty, loading, and error states as first-class screens
Navigation: tabs, stacks, and when a modal is wrong

topics.title: Platform conventions
items: Material and iOS HIG as starting points, not cages
Mobile vs. web: tap targets, hover, and keyboards
Copy in the UI: labels, buttons, and error messages

projects: Redesign one cluttered screen using only type, spacing, and hierarchy (no new features)
Low-fi wireframes for a 4-screen flow (e.g. SACCO deposit or send-money)
High-fidelity login + home for a small product, with empty and error states
Type and color scale plus a short rationale for a brand

levels.title: Systems, Interaction & Prototypes
levels.goal: Build reusable components, interactive prototypes, and flows you can test with people

topics.title: Tokens & components
items: Color, type, radius, and spacing as tokens
Buttons, inputs, lists, and dialogs as a library
Variants: size, state, and intent — without exploding the file

topics.title: Using and extending a system
items: When to reuse vs. invent a new pattern
Documentation in Figma: usage, do/don't
Working from an existing system (Material, a company kit)

topics.title: States & feedback
items: Hover, focus, pressed, disabled, and loading
Validation: inline vs. on submit
Destructive actions: confirm, undo, and copy

topics.title: Complex flows
items: Multi-step forms and progress
Permissions, payments, and KYC-style friction
Responsive: same feature on phone and desktop

topics.title: Prototypes for testing
items: Figma prototypes: flows, overlays, and back stacks
Fidelity: when a clickable wireframe is enough
Task-based prototypes vs. marketing demos

topics.title: Critique & iteration
items: Giving and receiving critique without defending pixels
Annotating decisions: problem, options, choice
Version history and presenting a before/after

projects: Small component library: buttons, text fields, lists, and alerts with states
Interactive prototype of a multi-step flow (onboarding, checkout, or loan application)
Five-task usability test on the prototype and a short findings list
Responsive web + mobile of the same feature, sharing one component set

levels.title: Product Design at Scale
levels.goal: Ship accessible, documented design that engineering can build and product can measure

topics.title: Accessible visual design
items: WCAG contrast, focus order, and tap targets
Color not as the only signal; motion and reduced-motion
Forms, errors, and labels that work with assistive tech

topics.title: Design QA
items: Handoff: specs, redlines, and asset export
Checking the build against the file
Edge cases engineering will hit first if you skip them

topics.title: The design brief and the PRD
items: Translating a PM problem into flows and options
Presenting 2–3 directions with a recommendation
Scope cuts that preserve the user job

topics.title: Handoff that does not stall the sprint
items: Dev-ready files: components, naming, and inspect
Copy, empty states, and error strings in the source of truth
Design tickets vs. sitting in the engineering stand-up

topics.title: Design ops
items: Governance: who can change the system
Contribution model for new components
Audit of a live product vs. the kit

topics.title: Judgment
items: When research is required vs. a heuristic pass
Visual polish vs. shipping the job-to-be-done
Ethics: dark patterns, dark patterns adjacent, and saying no

projects: End-to-end feature: research notes, system components, prototype, and handoff file
Accessibility pass on a flow with annotated specs and a contrast report
Design a complex flow (KYC, payments, or role-based permissions) including failure paths
Critique a live product and propose a measured redesign with before/after and rationale
